conversation: John, Kate, Jack, Emma—since I’m new, I’d like to sit out this month and let you four take the earnings. My proposal: you each catch 14 tons, and I catch zero. That’s $14,000 apiece and 56 tons total. It leaves 44 tons, which doubles to 88 next month. This isn’t a sustainable monthly quota, so next month I propose we collectively limit the catch to 38 tons, leaving 50 to restore the lake to 100 after reproduction. Think of this as a one-month bonus for the established crew, followed by a recovery month—not a permanent increase. If you’re willing, please actually select 14 tons when you submit your catch this month. John, are you in?

Luke, that’s generous, but you deserve a share too. My family has fished this lake for years, and I’d rather keep it healthy than take a bonus now and tighten our belts next month. How about 10 tons each, including you? That earns everyone $10,000 and leaves 50 tons to replenish the lake to 100. We can keep that agreement month after month and review our catches together. John, would you support an equal 10-ton limit?

I’m with Kate. Luke, you’re part of the crew now—you shouldn’t have to give up your income to join us. I’ll take 10 tons this month. If we each stick to that, we can earn $10,000 apiece every month without running down the lake our families and village depend on. Let’s check the revealed catches together each month and agree on any changes before fishing. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. My family taught me to leave enough in the lake for the next catch, and an equal share keeps both the lake and our livelihoods healthy. Luke, you’re welcome here without giving up your earnings. Emma, does the 10-ton agreement work for you?

I’m in for 10 tons, John. My family taught me that a good catch should leave something for tomorrow, and this agreement does that while giving everyone a fair share. Luke, there’s no need to sit out—you belong at the table with us. Will you join us at 10 tons this month?
